text:
maria: Heads up — the longstride KV cache bench is showing steady memory growth on the 16k-context synthetic run. Repro on my laptop and CI.

maria: Ran 1.0.7 build with --kv-alloc=compact and the growth still appears after ~1.1M tokens. Not a one-off spike, it's linear-ish.

alex: ugh. Can you paste the bench command + config?

maria: sure — command I used:
```
./tools/kv-bench --model t5-xxl --context 16384 --tokens 1200000 --stride 1024 --workload synthetic-longstride --kv-alloc compact --batching auto --kernel-hint auto
```
Output tail:
```
[INFO] token=1100000 mem_rss=18.3G kv_alloc=5.9G evict_ops=2
[INFO] token=1150000 mem_rss=19.1G kv_alloc=6.0G evict_ops=2
[INFO] token=1200000 mem_rss=19.9G kv_alloc=6.1G evict_ops=2
```
Small repro attached in the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/maria-longstride-repro

alex: interesting — evict_ops is low despite KV alloc rising. That suggests reuse isn't happening, or fragmentation prevents malloc reuse. Did you instrument slab/extent stats?

maria: nv — I enabled slab telemetry: active_extents keeps growing, free_extents stays flat. Fragmentation metric (waste_ratio) creeping from 0.06 -> 0.23.

jaime: pinging perf-bot to run the CI harness with kernel selection pinned. Might be interaction between GPU kernel memcpy paths and allocator behavior.

perf-bot: scheduled kvcache-longstride-ci on runner-09 with env KERNEL_SELECT=stable, KV_PREFETCH=0. Results ETA ~20m.

alex: also try running with --kernel-hint kernel=old-copy (forces legacy memcpy) and --batching=max-small to rule out batching-induced holder refs.

maria: will run both. quick note: heap profiler snapshot at 1.2M shows many ~64k fragments held by KV nodes with odd alignments (addresses not page-aligned). Might be GPU direct allocation rounding up.

alex: that aligns with hypothesis: if kernel uses pinned buffers, we might be hitting page-level allocations that fragment arena. If allocator can't coalesce, reuse fails, causing growth.

jaime: if we confirm kernel path causes different buffer alignment, we should add a test that asserts max waste_ratio < 0.15 after 500k tokens for longstride. That can catch regressions.

maria: test idea: synthetic suite variant longstride-compact-check that runs 500k tokens, reports waste_ratio, eviction_count, kv_reuse_hits. Fail CI if waste_ratio > 0.15 or kv_reuse_hits < 0.8.

alex: agree. Also log kernel selection tag and batching policy in the run metadata so we can correlate. Add a small flamegraph dump every 100k tokens (perf sampling) to see hot paths (memcpy vs gc).

perf-bot: CI run complete: runner-09: sustained growth reproduced. Kernel=stable shows more fragmentation than Kernel=old-copy. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/test/1934567890/artifacts

maria: uploaded my local flamegraphs to the CI artifacts. The stable kernel shows heavy time in gpu_dma_copy + allocator::alloc_extent. Legacy kernel spends more time in fast-path memcpy but less allocator churn.

alex: next steps: 1) Add longstride-compact-check regtest to synthetic suite 2) Add telemetry for kernel-tagged extent alignment 3) Try small patch to align allocations to page-size when pinned=true to see if coalescing improves reuse.

jaime: I'll own adding the regtest and gating in the CI. maria can prototype the alignment change and run perf. alex will triage kernel team if needed.

maria: starting a branch: kvcache/align-pinned-extents. I'll post a short PR with microbench results.

alex: thanks — great triage. If we see improvement, we can backport to the 1.0.x patch line and add the regression test.

maria: FYI — added the minimal repro as slack thread gist and annotated commands to rerun with perf sampling. Will ping when the PR is ready for review. :thumbsup:

jaime: marking this for 1.1.0 regression suite. Can someone add a short description to the test matrix entry?

maria: done — test matrix entry: "kvcache-longstride-compact-check: synthetic long context stride workload to detect allocator fragmentation and KV reuse regressions. Thresholds: waste_ratio<0.15, kv_reuse>=0.8"

alex: perfect. Closing loop once PR lands and CI passes.

perf-bot: note: flakiness observed on runner-03 historically for this workload. Use runner-09/14 for stable results.
